topic.title: Information sufficiency and measured cost of strong history representations
topic.question: Can a simpler representation of the same visible history retain the frozen joint_identity reference's predictive utility at lower measured training or inference cost, and which history relationships are necessary for that utility?
topic.hypothesis: The joint_identity result motivates a utility-retention study but does not establish event binding as its mechanism. Compact summaries may retain its utility at lower cost. Compare replacements against frozen joint_identity and DIN, including matched-capacity controls and category-brand pairing disruption that preserves field marginals and behavior/age information. A selective loss after disruption would provisionally support a role for pairing; equal losses under generic disruption or capacity controls would weaken that explanation. Failure to retain utility with cheaper summaries would reject those implementations, not prove that compression is impossible. Repeat promising contrasts within the remaining budget and assess uncertainty before claiming retained utility or a mechanism.
